title: Direct Connect and Site-to-Site VPN: the road in from the datacentre

videos.script: The shop still has an office, and in the office a rack of servers that will not move to AWS this year. {{office}} Those servers need to reach the VPC, privately, and the VPC needs to reach them. This lesson is about the road between the two. {{roads}} There are two kinds of road. The first is a VPN. It is an encrypted tunnel across the ordinary internet, ready in an afternoon, and cheap. {{tunnels}} AWS always gives you two tunnels, in two places, so that its own maintenance never cuts you off. {{dx}} The second road is Direct Connect. It is a physical cable from your router into AWS's, in a building in São Paulo where both of you have equipment. It takes weeks to order, and it does not cross the internet at all. {{moto}} moto can record both, and carries nothing down either. So the lesson builds what moto accepts, quotes what it answers, and says plainly which parts come from AWS's documentation. {{price}} Then the price list decides between them. A tunnel costs a few cents an hour, a port costs more, and the gigabytes going out are where they part. {{end}}
